## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A very brief single-juan dhāraṇī ascribed to [法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2) Fǎxián at the Sòng 譯經院. The text proper is the spell-formula alone, without the conventional sūtra-frame. It is a *jātismara* / *pūrvanivāsānusmṛti* dhāraṇī — i.e. a spell for the recollection of past lives.

**Abstract**

The text consists exclusively of an invocation: homage to Akṣobhya (阿芻毘夜 *Akṣobhya*), the Tathāgata, the Worthy One, the Fully-and-Perfectly Awakened, followed by the spell *oṃ akṣaye akṣaye akṣayāvaraṇa viśodhane svāhā*. The mantra-formula thus appeals to the *imperishable* (*akṣaya*) quality of Akṣobhya as the metaphysical ground for breaking through the karmic obscurations that veil memory of prior births. The companion text [KR6j0615](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0615) (T1383) provides the same spell within an Ānanda-frame and thereby supplies the narrative motivation: a thousand-aeons' karmic burden may be wiped clear, and seven *koṭi*-births' worth of past-life knowledge attained. Recorded in the *Dà-zhōng-xiángfú fǎbǎo lù*; Nanjio N0914.
